title: alert
description: Robot -> client operator alert. STATE, not a one-shot toast: a later frame with the same `code` replaces the earlier one, and `active: false` clears it. Additive to v1 -- older clients ignore the unknown type. Schema'd 2026-08-20, descriptively, from the L3 gateway's emitter (the thermal-supervisor stack shipped the frame first; this repo caught up). The frame is generic on purpose: `code` is the machine key a client dedupes and clears on, `severity` is the only rendering input, and everything condition-specific rides optional context fields, so a new alert kind is a new `code` value, not a new message type.

code.description: Stable machine key for the condition, e.g. "servo_thermal". Client behaviour keys on this, never on `message`. A client MUST ignore a code it does not recognise (render `message` at `severity`, nothing more), so a new robot can alert about conditions this client has never heard of.

severity.description: Rendering severity. The clear frame for a condition typically arrives as `info` with `active: false`.

active.description: true while the condition holds; false clears the same `code`. Because the control channel is unreliable AND unordered, a robot SHOULD re-emit the current alert state on change and MAY rebroadcast it; clients must treat frames as idempotent state, not events to count.

latched.description: Motion is inhibited by this condition and will not resume on the condition clearing alone (e.g. thermal lockout: the operator reconnects after cool-down). Absent means false.

message.description: Human-readable detail, rendered verbatim. Never parse it: anything a client needs to branch on belongs in `code` or a context field.

ts_ns.description: Robot monotonic/epoch ns, same clock as telemetry.ts_ns.

hottest_c.description: Thermal context: hottest servo case temperature in WHOLE degrees C -- same rounding contract as telemetry.servo_temps, for the same reason (the register is an integer).

joint.description: Thermal context: the joint the reading belongs to, in the robot's telemetry naming.
